findings.where: "Where we're starting" section: the Canggu, Uluwatu and Kuta Lombok destination cards and their "Best hostels >" lines, on desktop and phone
findings.fault: The cards look clickable but do nothing. Each is a raised white box with a hover rule and a link-coloured "Best hostels" label with a chevron. In the DOM all three are static, so no destination guide can be reached from this page. The hero's "Explore destinations" button and the nav's "Destinations" link only scroll down to these dead cards, so the page cannot do one of its three jobs.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who taps "Best hostels" for Canggu or Uluwatu while planning the next hop. Nothing happens, they decide the site is broken or empty, and they go back to the sites they already use.

findings.where: Nav bar "How we rank" (desktop, and behind Menu on phone) and the same link in the footer
findings.fault: Both "How we rank" links point back to this same page, and the page has no ranking explanation. The one link that backs up the hero's "ranks on merit alone" claim goes nowhere.
findings.who_objects: A traveller who doubts a new site's "merit alone" claim and clicks to see the method. They land back where they started, which makes the claim look empty on a product whose case rests on published, trustworthy ranking.

findings.fault: All three are styled as links but go back to this page, so no privacy notice, terms or reporting route exists. The page still asks visitors for contact details through its launch-news action.
findings.who_objects: A visitor deciding whether to hand over their email for launch news, who checks the privacy policy first and finds nothing. A hostel owner who wants to report wrong content and has no route.

findings.where: Hero primary button "Email luc@mantahostels.com for launch news"
findings.fault: The page's main action, signing up for launch news, is a mailto link. Nothing is collected on the page. On a desktop or browser with no mail app set up, the click does nothing or opens an unfamiliar app. The visitor then has to write their own email asking to be told about the launch, so the sign-up only half works.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who wants launch news and expects a one-step sign-up. They click, nothing useful opens or they face a blank email, and they give up. That loses the contacts the page exists to collect.

findings.where: Nav bar links "Destinations" and "How we rank" (desktop)
findings.fault: Two nav links of the same kind look different: "How we rank" is underlined and "Destinations" is not. The difference reads as a state, such as the current page or a different kind of link, but there is no such difference.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning the nav who takes the underlined item as the page they are already on, or as the only real link. It is minor, but the nav no longer tells them where they are.

findings.fault: The footer wordmark looks the same as the header wordmark, which is a home link, but in the footer it is static. One look carries two functions.
findings.who_objects: A visitor at the bottom of a long phone scroll who taps the footer logo to get back to the top or home, as most sites allow, and gets no response.
